question_text: A quad-core processor is running four independent programs. Each core uses an instruction pipeline with four stages: fetch, decode, execute and write-back. Describe how pipelining within each core, together with the cores working in parallel, improves the overall performance of the system.
adaptation_rationale: Original question written by Claude (single-agent Chunk 3 continuation, 2026-11-04) for a syllabus statement with no linked question at handover; no historical source question or official marking status claimed.
solution: While one instruction is being executed, the next has already been decoded and the one after that fetched, so the four stages work on different instructions at the same time. Once the pipeline is full, one instruction can complete (write back its result) every clock cycle instead of every four cycles, so throughput rises even though each individual instruction still passes through all four stages. Each core has its own pipeline and works independently, so the four programs are processed simultaneously on different cores. Overall, many more instructions are completed per unit of time (up to about four times the single-core pipelined rate), provided the programs are independent and the pipelines are not stalled.

marking_points.criterion: Explains that the fetch, decode, execute and write-back stages operate on different instructions at the same time (overlapping instructions).
States that once the pipeline is full about one instruction completes per clock cycle, increasing throughput (latency of a single instruction is not reduced).
Describes each core fetching and executing its own instruction stream independently, so the programs run in parallel on separate cores.
Links both mechanisms to more instructions completed per unit time overall, with a valid condition (independent programs / no stalls or dependencies).

acceptable_alternatives: Accept a correct labelled timing diagram for the overlap point. Accept "throughput" or "instructions per cycle" wording. Do not require hazard terminology.
partial_credit_notes: Award each independent point once, up to 4 marks. Accept equivalent correct wording or valid alternative code. Do not double-credit one idea.

verification.technical: Manual author check of every criterion against the exact statement and all guidance paragraphs; no executable component.
verification.scope: Does not assess pipeline hazards, branch prediction or cache coherence (not required by the guidance). Speed-up figure is an idealised upper bound.
